trap-superlative.notes: REPORT ONLY, not fixed (math + doctrine). FOUR findings. (1) The machine-epsilon claim is refuted by the block's own cited witness, same defect as q-hecke-seminormal-character-closure.md: Table 1 prints |tr_M| = 1.0653062286 / 0.9232332972 / 0.3882864715 / 0.1040521187 / 0.2065408586 with rel errs ~1e-15, while computations/tr-m-q-hecke-seminormal.witness.json records 1.14575978 / 0.98774376 / 0.57517233 / 0.22931015 / 0.40376714 with rel errs 7.8e-8 / 6.9e-8 / 1.5e-7 / 1.9e-7 / 2.5e-7. Seven orders of magnitude, and the witness's own assertions gate only at 1e-3 and 1e-6. .ts status is 'verified'. (2) CAL DOCTRINE SLIP: 'using only the electron mass (CAL-1) and the substrate parameter q_0 (CAL-2)'. Per AGENTS.md CAL-2 is the decay width D_beta, whose numerical PROXY is Q_beta; q_0 is pinned BY CAL-2, it is not CAL-2. And 'we do not use Q_beta as an input. Rather, Q_beta becomes an output' overstates: AGENTS.md states plainly that Q_beta reproduced from q_0 is a 0.17% CROSS-CHECK, 'not a fourth input' -- the honest framing under the ideal 3-CAL. (Under the 2026-08-07 proton pin it IS a prediction, but then q_0 is not CAL-2 either; the block cannot have it both ways.) (3) TABLE 3 SIGN ERROR: the Net row gives Delta_i = h(h-2)/2 = -0.18722 and E_0 = 4.18598 MeV, so the Delta_i*E_0 entry is -0.7836, printed '+0.7836' -- and the column's own three preceding entries (+0.0915, -0.4376, -0.4376) sum to -0.7837. (4) EVERYTHING ELSE RECOMPUTED AND CORRECT, do not re-flag: Q_beta = m_e|q_0^2-2q_0-1|(q_0+1)/(2q_0^3) = 0.7836458 MeV; h = 0.2090603, h^2/2 = 0.0218531, -h/2 = -0.1045301, E_0 = 4.1859814, per-channel products 0.09148 / -0.43757; the 6-term 0.18829*E_0 = 0.788178 = the quoted 0.7882 and its +0.747%; the tightening factor 0.747/0.168 = 4.45; the pole identities 18(1)+21(0)+1 = 19 and 18(1)+21(1)+1 = 40; and EVERY cell of Table 2 (D 938.272088+939.565421 = 1877.837509, Delta +2.224566, +0.1186%; T 2817.402929, +8.481796, +0.3020%; He-3 2816.109597, +7.717990, +0.2748%; He-4 3755.675017, +28.295639, +0.7591%), all six CODATA reference masses, and all four binding values. PIN NOTE: Q_beta = 0.7836458 is IDENTICAL to 8 digits at the proton, muon and old-muon pins, so 0.7836 discriminates none of them (it does exclude the erroneous 1.1097, which gives 0.784157).
